gaps.note: Mainnet Monad runs 0.16.7, not 0.16.5. The theme-monad-shipped-binary verifier fetched https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/full-node-installation on 2026-11-26 and found monad_version 0.16.7 for mainnet and testnet, and rpc.monad.xyz answers Monad/0.16.7. The research unit downloaded the 0.16.5 package and read its Task 4 gas rules (x86.cpp:443-448, emitter.cpp:1030-1046 and 1284-1298, runtime/call.cpp:136-154, runtime/storage.cpp:70-73, runtime/context.cpp:174-176) at v0.16.5. OPCODES.md Check 4 still names v0.16.5 as what Monad runs. The two Task 4 clearances and every compiled-path reading made only at v0.16.5 need a reread at v0.16.7, or a statement that those files are byte equal between the tags.

No file of the shipped Monad validator package has been read. The unit stopped because no zstd decoder was available and a source build of zstd was refused. node v22.23.5 is installed in this environment and exposes zlib.zstdDecompressSync (checked on 2026-11-26), so the data.tar.zst of the .deb can be decompressed with a tool already present. The lead stays open for a reason that no longer holds.

The Pocket gateway for Ethereum rotates reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc and reth/v2.10.1-58ebce1 (theme-stateful-interpreter Task 3 brackets, and a critic query on 2026-11-26 that got both in two calls). The Cargo.lock at reth 58ebce1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/58ebce1/Cargo.lock, fetched 2026-11-26) resolves evm2 through a [patch] entry to git rev 01df8f6a396d0250da286cb763faa6ec292d65b5 with ruint 1.21.1. No file under state/ names evm2 rev 01df8f6a. The OPCODES.md client table lists only reth v2.11.0 on evm2 66687c18. Cycle 24 pinned only 77 of 310 battery and targeted calls to v2.10.1. One build that answers Ethereum calls runs an interpreter revision nobody has read.

The Ethereum RPC in state/networks.json (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com) now answers web3_clientVersion with a Cloudflare challenge page (ethereum-reference and theme-deferred-verification both recorded it on 2026-11-26). The reference endpoint behind most Ethereum words of earlier cycles is no longer reachable from this environment. eth.drpc.org names no build (Geth/v10.0.0/drpc) and Pocket rotates two builds. networks.json needs an Ethereum endpoint that both answers and names its build, or each Ethereum word must be pinned per call on Pocket.

theme-stateful-interpreter reports that all 199 calls equal the reference. Its verifier read out/compare.json and found Tempo at 6 of 10 rows, with 3 mismatches and 1 error: a64 steps 4 to 5 and d300 revert with empty data at the 25,000,000 gas Tempo grants, and e reverts with WrappedError from afterSwap after an out of gas. The research text says e gives the same ten words on every network, which Tempo's row does not show. So Tempo, a one-client network on the rewritten ruint 1.21.1 paths, has no word-level comparison for the long alternating-denominator sequences, which were the point of the theme.

One inference in the theme-hook-and-native-sides precompile item is unsound. It reads a successful value call with empty input at 0x100 as proof that no P-256 precompile is there. On Ethereum the same call succeeds with empty output: a critic eth_call from the PoolManager address with value 1 and empty input to 0x100 returned 0x on reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc (eth.api.pocket.network) and on eth.drpc.org on 2026-11-26, while 0x0b and 0x11 failed. For 0x100 the behaviour matches Ethereum and says nothing about the precompile. The item also limits the Polygon 0x0a result to the drpc gateway. The same call to 0x0a returned 0x on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor/a863b8e5cce1/v2.11.1-private), so bor itself has no point evaluation precompile at 0x0a. On api.avax.network 0x0a failed with invalid input length and 0x0b returned 0x, as the item says. None of this moves pool funds.

The seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas and MegaETH had no network unit in cycle 26. The OP Stack cells were last worked in cycle 24 and the MegaETH cells in cycle 25 (state/ledger.json). Cycle 26 reached them only through the four theme units, and every one of those ran eth_call on the RPC path. MegaETH's endpoint is a replica that applies the sequencer's results without running them (cycle 25), so cycle 26 adds nothing about the closed MegaETH producer.

reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f answers bsc-rpc.publicnode.com again. Cycle 24 compared only its Cargo.lock with v0.1.4 and recorded that its own source files could not be listed or compared. Whatever reth-bsc changes in its own crates (instruction table, precompile set, system calls before or after user transactions) is unread. The battery matches on it, so the gap concerns block execution paths that eth_call does not take.

leads.question: With harness.cpp changed so that exec_code keeps its own copy of the code for the life of the frame (or with the harness run under Valgrind, as theme-monad-shipped-binary did for cases 1369 and 1528), do the 13 hook-failure cases of cycles/026/theme-hook-and-native-sides.work/out/hx/rep/diffcases.json and sequences d40 and d300 of theme-stateful-interpreter give SAME in the interpreter and native code at v0.16.7 and v0.16.5, and equal the reference words?
leads.why: These are the only open differences between Monad's two engines on PoolManager frames, and Monad validators run the PoolManager as native code. 12 of the 13 revert the whole unlock in native code only. If the harness fault explains them, the item closes. If any case survives, native code decides a failed hook call differently from the interpreter, and an ordinary account can send that call through a pool it creates.

leads.question: Decompress data.tar.zst of pool/main/monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb (SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb) with node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and ar and tar, without running any file from it. What do the execution library's .comment, build id and asmjit strings say? Are the debug-symbol emitter functions for SHL, SHR, SAR by a non-literal count, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, the comparisons, JUMPI and the memory check, and the uint256 runtime routines, equal to the cycle 23 0.16.7 harness objects, equal up to register allocation, or different? Repeat for 0.16.5 (sha256 0b27486f...acc8, already in dl/).
leads.why: Every compiled-path result on Monad rests on a local build with clang -O2. The tagged recipe builds with gcc-15 -march=haswell. The emitted code depends on the emitter and asmjit source, but the routines that the emitted code calls are compiled by gcc, and nobody has compared them. A differing routine would give validators a word that no eth_call shows.

leads.question: Are x86.cpp, emitter.cpp, emitter.hpp, runtime/call.cpp, runtime/storage.cpp, runtime/context.cpp, the uint256 headers and the varcode cache byte equal between the Monad v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 tags? For every file that differs, does the reading of theme-monad-shipped-binary Task 4 (block base gas on entry, deferred sign check, base gas added back before CALL and SSTORE) still hold at v0.16.7?
leads.why: Mainnet runs 0.16.7 and the Task 4 clearance was read at 0.16.5. A change between the tags in where an out of gas or a stack check fires inside a block could make the two engines differ on a PoolManager frame.

leads.question: cycles/026/theme-hook-and-native-sides.work/out/coverage.json lists 203 jump sides that no case of cycles 25 or 26 ran. Among them are SqrtPriceMath.sol:37, 59, 109, 135, 164, 194 and 197, FullMath.sol:33 and 112, TickMath.sol:33 and 70, and SafeCast.sol:18 and 50. Intersect them with research/network-risk/opcodes/coverage.json (script sets 1 to 6) and the cycle 24 producer coverage. Which math side has never run on any network by any set, and does a case built for it return the reference words on all 21?
leads.why: These sides hold the overflow and rounding branches where an integer library fault would show up. Coverage is reported per cycle, so it is not clear whether some of them were never run anywhere.

leads.question: In the cycle 23 and 24 traces of mined MegaETH and HyperEVM PoolManager transactions, how many frames reached each arithmetic site with an edge operand: SAR by 255 and SIGNEXTEND of a negative tick (TickMath.sol:61-63), SDIV and SMOD of a negative compressed tick (TickBitmap.sol:20-26), mulmod(a, b, not(0)) with prod1 nonzero (FullMath.sol:24-33), and the round-up mulmod in mulDivRoundingUp (FullMath.sol:112)?
leads.why: On these two networks the producer is closed and eth_call runs a replica, so mined transactions are the only evidence about the code that writes blocks. Cycle 24 counted jump sides, not operand edges. A JIT that specializes on literal operands could be wrong only on an edge operand that no mined frame has used.

leads.question: Read the nanoreth rule that classifies a legacy transaction with gas price 0 as a system transaction and takes its sender from s. In the blocks since the MRB fork, is every gas-price-0 transaction's derived sender a HyperCore system address (0x2222...2222 or 0x20...-prefixed)? Does any public HyperEVM RPC accept such a transaction at eth_estimateGas or eth_call with the PoolManager as the derived sender?
leads.why: If the producer applied the same rule to a user-submitted transaction, anyone could send as the PoolManager and move every pooled balance, a critical in-scope path. Cycle 24 found 4,620 such transactions in 12,000 blocks, all from system addresses, but nobody has read the rule or checked the blocks after the fork.

leads.question: F-020 remains plausible. One fact would settle it: can the treasury address of an aligned quote asset be set, or changed after activation, to an address that has EVM code without a validator vote? Read the HyperCore action that sets it and any published validation of that field.
leads.why: It decides whether the least privileged party is the validator set (operator) or the token deployer (issuer). Neither is in scope, but the ledger should not carry a plausible high finding for the wrong actor.

leads.question: Which contract declares the error selector 0xcea9e31d that the failed Avalanche transaction of L-1097 returns after its own block? Read the verified source of the target 0x6a000f20005980200259b80c5102003040001068 and the routers it calls. Does the revert come from that contract after the PoolManager returned?
leads.why: This closes L-1097 without a trace endpoint. No error in src/ has the selector, so a PoolManager decision that differs from the source is unlikely, but it is not excluded.

leads.question: On an erigon v3.8.1 backend pinned by web3_clientVersion on both sides of each call, does sequence c2 of theme-stateful-interpreter (a beforeSwap hook writes slot0 between src/PoolManager.sol:196 and the read in Pool.swap) return the reference words?

leads.question: Like Robinhood Chain's official endpoint and the Pocket gateways for Arbitrum One and Ethereum, does any other networks.json endpoint route single requests or batch elements to different builds or architectures? Send 30 three-element web3_clientVersion batches to each and record mixed answers.
leads.why: Several cycles pinned eth_call results to a build by brackets that assume one backend per batch. Robinhood Chain shows that this assumption can fail, and any network where it fails has unpinned evidence.

leads.question: Do MegaETH (realtime or mini-block state) and HyperEVM serve balances, call results or receipts at latest from a block that consensus or the sequencer can still drop, as theme-deferred-verification found for Monad's proposed blocks?
leads.why: The Monad finding is an operator-level integration hazard. The same shape on the two other fast-block networks was not checked.
